clue.text: A fairy to quarrel endlessly? It could be the sherry!

indicators.note: without an end, so the word for quarrel loses its final letter

blocks.note: taken as written
a peri is a fairy or sprite of Persian legend
a tiff is a petty quarrel

explanation.surface: Someone asks what a fairy might drink before a squabble, and the answer is a glass of sherry.
explanation.walkthrough: APERITIF: PERI is a crossword favourite for a fairy, and TIFF with its last F dropped completes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherry is a classic drink served before dinner to stimulate appetite, so it is one example of the category.

clue.text: This clue is not a hard thing to bear

definitions.note: the definition is a sentence fragment pointing at the clue's own direction

blocks.note: taken as written
a cross to bear is a burden

explanation.surface: A wry remark that this puzzle is no great burden to endure.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue refers to itself: it is 1 Down, so it is not the other direction in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Being a Down clue, this entry is self-evidently the opposite of a horizontal one, hence the joke.

clue.text: Finally the son has lark — one getting away

indicators.note: finally points to the very last letter of the following word

blocks.note: last letter of the word
S is the abbreviation for son
a lark or caper is a prank

explanation.surface: At last the boy has some fun, and someone makes a run for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who escapes is a fugitive breaking free from captivity.

clue.text: Doing well, friend lacking airs and graces

blocks.note: in form means performing well
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A friend who is doing well but has no pretensions.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting casually, without ceremony or pretension, is behaving without stiff manners.

clue.text: I will start to cheer on team, looking embarrassed and foolish?

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter only

blocks.note: contracted to I'll
first letter of the word
taken as written
a side is a team
red in the face from embarrassment

explanation.surface: A fan vows to cheer the team on, then looks sheepish and silly.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-considered means badly thought out, which makes an action unwise or rash.

clue.text: Trainee protecting the female child looking innocent

indicators.note: to protect something is to wrap around it, so one piece sits around the other

blocks.note: a cub is a novice, as in cub reporter
the pronoun for a female

explanation.surface: A trainee shields a little girl who looks blameless.
explanation.definitionFit: A cherub is a chubby angelic infant in art, used of any sweet-faced, innocent-seeming youngster.

clue.text: Greeting that comes from above

blocks.note: first meaning: a salutation
second meaning: frozen pellets falling from the sky

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a heavenly salutation; the second sense is weather.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an old salutation and also the icy precipitation that drops from clouds.

clue.text: Went berserk in rave outside port

indicators.note: outside means the first word wraps around the second

blocks.note: to rave is to rant
Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian port

explanation.surface: Someone loses control at a party outside a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rave' looks like a party but works as a verb meaning to shout wildly.
explanation.definitionFit: To run riot is to behave wildly and uncontrollably, the same as going berserk.

clue.text: I attempt to follow gang in criminal activity

indicators.note: to follow is to come after, so these pieces go behind the next one

blocks.note: a band is a group or gang
taken as written
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: A recruit tries to join a gang in its crimes.
explanation.definitionFit: Banditry is robbery by outlaws, a form of lawless conduct.

clue.text: Big bird to be unsteady, mostly

indicators.note: mostly means not all of it, so the final letter of the word is dropped

blocks.note: to rock is to sway or wobble

explanation.surface: A large bird totters on its feet.
explanation.walkthrough: ROCK loses its K to leave ROC.
explanation.definitionFit: The roc is a gigantic mythical bird from Arabian tales, said to carry off elephants.

clue.text: Men go in lift possibly to get what restaurant offers?

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of several arrangements, so these letters may be rearranged

blocks.note: the eleven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Diners ride an elevator up to reach a rooftop restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: Filet mignon is a prized tender beef steak cut, a typical item on a restaurant menu.

clue.text: Criticise act to sell multiple raffle tickets?

definitions.text: act to sell multiple raffle tickets?

blocks.note: first meaning: to scold someone severely

blocks.clueFragment: act to sell multiple raffle tickets?
blocks.note: second meaning, taken literally: detaching a run of joined tickets from the book

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for a dressing-down is read literally as pulling off a row of joined raffle tickets.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to rebuke angrily, while literally it describes ripping a strip of tickets free.

clue.text: Star full of power, or police officer without staff

blocks.note: short for superintendent
W/O is the abbreviation for without
to man or staff a post

explanation.surface: A choice between a powerful celebrity and a police officer who has no team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' looks like a noun but works as the verb meaning to provide people for.
explanation.definitionFit: Superwoman is the comic-book heroine with superhuman strength, a star figure endowed with great powers.

clue.text: Monkey: one pursuing bird

indicators.note: pursuing means coming behind, so this piece is placed after the other

blocks.note: a tit is a small songbird
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A monkey chases after a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The titi is a small long-tailed South American primate species.

clue.text: Religious rite in river is working

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one word sits within the other

blocks.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall
unction is anointing with oil as a sacrament

explanation.surface: A baptism held in a river is going ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Something functional is operational and doing its job, i.e. in running order.

clue.text: Narrow thoroughfares or wide streams?

blocks.note: first meaning: the minor roads of Britain's numbering system, often narrow lanes
second meaning: the wide shallow waterways of Norfolk and Suffolk

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, B roads are minor roads, a grade below A roads; the Norfolk Broads are a network of wide rivers and lakes in eastern England. The clue sets narrow against wide for fun.
explanation.definitionFit: Split in two, the word gives minor British country lanes; whole, it names the wide East Anglian lakes and rivers.

clue.text: Neighbour needs a dairy product

blocks.note: taken as written
butter is made from cream

explanation.surface: The person next door needs some butter.
explanation.definitionFit: One who abuts is adjacent, sharing a boundary, so a bordering property owner is a neighbour.

clue.text: Puts up with relations in furry attire

blocks.note: to bear is to tolerate
kin are relatives

explanation.surface: Someone tolerates family members dressed in fur.
explanation.walkthrough: A bearskin is the tall fur cap of the British Foot Guards.
explanation.definitionFit: A bearskin is a tall fur hat worn by guardsmen, so it is headgear made of fur.

clue.text: Half of them were not well and sent message

indicators.note: only half of the word survives, so its first two letters are removed

blocks.note: taken as written before being halved
to ail is to be sick

explanation.surface: Half the group were ill and sent a note.
explanation.walkthrough: The back half of THEM is EM.
explanation.definitionFit: To email is to send an electronic communication, so the past tense matches having sent one.

clue.text: Instrument old character used to accompany Jolson?

indicators.note: accompanying means going alongside, so the pieces sit together side by side

blocks.note: Al Jolson, the American singer
thorn is an Old English letter

explanation.surface: An old-timer backs singer Al Jolson on a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: Thorn is the letter þ used in Old English; 'old character' looks like a person.
explanation.definitionFit: An althorn is a valved brass horn in the saxhorn family.

clue.text: Tommy, for one, given food with little hesitation

blocks.note: tuck is British slang for food, especially snacks at school
er is the short sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: Someone named Tommy is handed food after a brief pause.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Tommy Tucker is a nursery-rhyme boy who sings for his supper, so 'little' in the clue nods to him.
explanation.definitionFit: Tommy is one bearer of the surname in the nursery rhyme, so he is an example.

clue.text: Smart English member meeting one from a colony?

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
a limb is a member of the body
ants live in colonies

explanation.surface: A sharp English MP meets a settler from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'colony' suggests empire; here it is an ants' nest.
explanation.definitionFit: Smart in the sense of stylish and well dressed, which is graceful in appearance.

clue.text: Little old gentleman is a god

blocks.note: O is the short form of old
the title for a gentleman
taken as written

explanation.surface: A small elderly man is revered as divine.
explanation.definitionFit: Osiris is the Egyptian deity of the afterlife and the underworld.

clue.text: Hotel‘s documents read out

blocks.note: writs are formal legal documents

explanation.surface: A hotel's paperwork is read aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ritz is a famous luxury London establishment for guests, named after César Ritz.

clue.text: Craftspeople needing skill if joining top decorators

blocks.note: art is skill, as in the art of persuasion
taken as written
icers decorate the tops of cakes

explanation.surface: Craftsmen need skill when working alongside leading decorators.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top decorators' reads as the best in the trade but means those who put icing on top of cakes.

clue.text: Island‘s broadcaster picked up

indicators.note: picked up as a radio signal is, meaning heard rather than seen

blocks.note: Sky is a British satellite television company

clue.text: Like sale article at ground level?

blocks.note: first meaning: reduced in price, as goods in a sale are
second meaning: felled or flattened onto the floor

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that one phrase covers both a cut price and something literally floored.

blocks.note: nan is an informal word for grandmother

clue.text: Creative impulse of a female, calm American

blocks.note: taken as written

flat water is calm
US for the United States
